title: How Can We Help? Owl Helpers Start Here

leo.name: Leo
leo.persona: playful 9-year-old boy, always a little messy, friendly

focusWords.kidDefinition: When people talk together about an idea or problem.
examples: We have a discussion about our school garden.
Let's have a discussion about helping at home.

focusWords.kidDefinition: A picture with rows and boxes that shows information.
examples: Let's make a chart with our chores.
The chart shows who sweeps on Monday.

focusWords.kidDefinition: To give an idea for someone to think about.
examples: I suggest we water the plants at school.
Can I suggest a fun way to help?

focusWords.kidDefinition: To clean the floor with a broom.
examples: Dad sweeps the kitchen every Saturday morning.
I sweep the floor after lunch.

focusWords.kidDefinition: To tidy your sheets and blanket on the bed.
examples: I make the bed every morning.
Leo makes the bed before breakfast.

focusWords.kidDefinition: To pour water on plants so they can grow.
examples: Mom waters the plants in the afternoon.
Please water the flowers in the garden.

focusWords.kidDefinition: To put plates, forks and cups on the table for a meal.
examples: My little sister sets the table for lunch.
We set the table before dinner.

focusWords.kidDefinition: To give things to people who need them, for free.
examples: Let's donate our old toys to the animal shelter.
We can donate books to the library.

focusWords.kidDefinition: To use old things again, so they are not thrown away.
examples: We recycle plastic bottles and cans.
Please recycle paper in the blue bin.

lines.text: Hello, friends! I am Lingo, your owl teacher.
Our school is a busy place with lots of people.
Who helps keep it clean, bright and happy?
Mia and Leo have a big question today.
How can we help our community?

question.text: What is one way you help at home?

prompt.text: We have a ____ about how we can help our community.

explain.text: A discussion is when people talk together about an idea.

prompt.text: Point to the word for rows and boxes that show our chores.

explain.text: A chart is a picture with rows and boxes that show information.

prompt.text: Listen: Can I suggest an idea? Which word did you hear?

explain.text: To suggest means to give an idea for others to think about.

prompt.text: Dad ____ the kitchen every Saturday morning.

explain.text: Sweeps means cleaning the floor with a broom.

prompt.text: To make the bed means to tidy your sheets and blanket. True or false?

explain.text: When you make the bed, you smooth the sheets and blanket.

prompt.text: Which word is the odd one out?

explain.text: Chart is a noun, but water, sweep and recycle are action words.

prompt.text: Mom ____ the plants in the afternoon.

explain.text: To water means to pour water on plants so they can grow.

prompt.text: Point to the words for putting plates and forks on the table.

explain.text: Set the table means to put plates, forks and cups out for a meal.

prompt.text: Donate means to keep something just for yourself. True or false?

explain.text: To donate means to give something to people who need it.
To recycle means to use old things again instead of throwing them away.

lines.text: Time for a quick owl quiz! Show me your best helping words.

prompt.text: Ask your partner: What chores do you do at home?

frames: I sometimes ___ the plants on Sunday.
I suggest we ___ together at school.

model.text: I make the bed every morning. I water the plants on Sunday. I suggest we recycle bottles at school.

lines.text: Brilliant work, everyone! You know so many helpful words.
You can now talk about chores, charts and good ideas.
Next lesson, we read about helping our community together.

exitTicket.text: Name one chore you can do at home.
Which word means giving things to people who need them?
